Austin is called a "naive empiricist" because he treats observable experience and ordinary sensory observation as a straightforward, reliable basis for knowledge, without adequately addressing skeptical doubt, theory-laden perception, or the inferential justification of empirical claims. The label is generally a criticism, suggesting he underestimates how much interpretation and background assumption shape observation. (Per the team note, the point may instead concern his pragmatic conception of laws as observable commands and habits of obedience rather than conceptual structures.)
CONFIDENCE: 55
